With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

page_token.description: list only: the `next_page_token` a listing of the same scope gave, to list the artifacts after it.

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (writing people will keep editing or pass around as text, such as a memo, plan, spec, proposal or notes), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a page to look at or use: an explainer, a diagram, anything interactive, a dashboard that shows data, a spreadsheet, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.description:

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

     2	
     3	Interview method for `grill` mode: settle every open decision with the user, recording terms and hard decisions as you go.
     4	
     5	Adapted from the `grilling` and `domain-modeling` skills by Matt Pocock: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills
     6	
     7	> MIT License. Copyright (c) 2026 Matt Pocock.

    10	> THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE.
    11	
    12	## Decision tree
    13	
    14	- Task = tree of decisions. A decision depends on others when its options only make sense once they are settled.
    15	- **Frontier** = open decisions whose prerequisites are all settled. Ask only the frontier; deeper questions wait for later rounds.
    16	- `grill <plan-path>`: tree = the plan's assumptions, open points, risky points. Settled `## Decisions` entries are not re-asked.
    17	
    18	## Facts vs decisions
    19	
    20	- Facts (what the code does, what exists, versions, conventions, test setup): look them up in the code, or with read-only exploration subagents. Never ask the user.
    21	- Decisions (what the user wants, trade-offs only they can weigh): ask.
    22	- Missing detail with an obvious default = not a question. Use the default; note it under Assumptions.
    23	
    24	## Rounds
    25	
    26	- Plain text only. No AskUserQuestion.
    27	- Each round: whole frontier, numbered `Q1..Qn`. Each question: one terse line + `Rec:` recommended answer (+ short why when not obvious).
    28	- Word recommendations so "yes" accepts all of them.
    29	- Reply rules, stated once at the end of the round: "yes" = accept all recs; override by number (e.g. `Q2: no, keep flat files`); unmentioned = rec accepted.
    30	- Then stop and wait for the reply.
    31	- Recommendations follow SKILL.md Plan step 3 "Do not overengineer": simplest option meeting the stated need, repo's existing tools/patterns, no speculative features or config.
    32	- Skip trivia: no question whose answer would not change the plan. A clear task may need one round or none.
    33	
    34	Format:
    35	```
    36	Round N
    37	Q1. <question>
    38	    Rec: <answer>
    39	Q2. ...
    40	Reply "yes" to accept all, or override by number.
    41	```
    42	
    43	## Domain modeling
    44	
    45	While grilling, sharpen the language:
    46	- Term used loosely, or two words for one thing → ask which one and what exactly it means.
    47	- Probe a term with a concrete edge-case scenario ("note edited after archiving: still archived?").
    48	- Check terms against existing code names and `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md`; flag conflicts.
    49	
    50	## Writing after every round
    51	
    52	After each answered round, before asking the next:
    53	1. Append the settled decisions to `## Decisions` in `poe/<slug>/plan.md` (one bullet each: decision + short why).
    54	2. Add or update glossary entries for terms resolved this round.
    55	3. Write an ADR for any decision that qualifies (below).
    56	
    57	Nothing settled lives only in the chat; `/clear` then `grill <plan-path>` must resume without re-asking.
    58	
    59	## Glossary
    60	
    61	- Path: `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md`. Create only when the first term is resolved.
    62	- Project-specific terms only. No generic programming words. No implementation detail (file names, classes, schemas).
    63	- Entry format:
    64	  ```
    65	  **Term**: 1–2 sentence definition.
    66	  _Avoid_: synonym, other synonym
    67	  ```
    68	- Keep entries alphabetical; edit an existing entry instead of adding a duplicate.
    69	
    70	## ADRs
    71	
    72	- Path: `poe/docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md`. Create `adr/` only when the first ADR is written.
    73	- Write one only when all three hold:
    74	  1. Hard to reverse (costly to change later).
    75	  2. Surprising (a future reader would ask "why this way?").
    76	  3. Real trade-off (viable alternatives were rejected).
    77	- Otherwise the decision lives only in `plan.md` `## Decisions`. Zero ADRs is normal.
    78	- Number = highest existing number + 1, 4 digits (`0001` if none). Slug = short kebab-case title.
    79	- Format:
    80	  ```
    81	  # NNNN: <Title>
    82	
    83	  <1–3 sentences: context, decision, why.>
    84	  ```
    85	  Add sections (Considered options, Consequences) only when they add real value.
    86	
    87	## Finish
    88	
    89	- Frontier empty → summarize understanding in ≤5 bullets; ask the user to confirm it matches theirs.
    90	- Correction → new round on the affected decisions.
    91	- Confirmed → grilling done; continue Grill mode in SKILL.md.
----
     1	---
     2	name: poe
     3	description: Plan, decompose, and execute complex coding or analysis tasks in phases using fresh-context subagents and file-based progress notes. Use when the user explicitly requests staged multi-agent work, context-conscious orchestration, or continuation of an existing phase plan.
     4	argument-hint: "[plan|grill|split|execute|resume|report] [task description or plan path]"
     5	disable-model-invocation: true
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Phase-Orchestrated Work
     9	
    10	User request: $ARGUMENTS
    11	
    12	You are the **orchestrator**. Keep the parent conversation focused on decisions, dependency management, integration, and verification. Delegate bounded implementation or research to fresh-context subagents rather than accumulating their intermediate work in the parent context.
    13	
    14	## Output style
    15	
    16	Be concise. Sacrifice grammar for the sake of concision.
    17	
    18	- Applies to every reply and every file poe writes for the user: `plan.md`, phase briefs, `status.md`, `summary.md`.
    19	- Bullets and fragments over prose.
    20	- Applies to every reply, including errors, failures, and answers to questions; put long content in files.
    21	- Never drop required content: acceptance criteria, risks, verification commands, exact file paths, test results, unknowns.
    22	
    23	## Operating modes
    24	
    25	- `plan <task>` (or a task description without a mode): write `plan.md` only, then stop so the user can review it. Do not split it into phases and do not edit implementation files.
    26	- `grill <task | plan-path>`: interview the user on open decisions, then write or update `plan.md` (see Grill mode). May write only `poe/<slug>/plan.md`, `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md`, and `poe/docs/adr/`; never implementation files.
    27	- `split [plan-path]`: split a reviewed `plan.md` into phases and work units, then stop for user approval. Do not edit implementation files.
    28	- `execute [plan-path]`: execute a plan that has been split and approved. If the plan has no phase briefs yet, say so and ask the user to run `split` first.
    29	- When a mode is given no path, use the unambiguous active plan in `poe/` (never `poe/docs/` or `poe/trash/`); otherwise ask for the path.
    30	- `resume [plan-path]`: read `status.md` and the progress notes, compare them with the actual files, tests, and git diff, reconcile discrepancies, and continue only incomplete approved work. When it finishes or stops, write `summary.md`, copy the logs, and build the report as in Execute mode step 9.
    31	- `report [plan-path]`: copy this session's logs as in the Logs section, build the report as in the Report section, and give the user the path of `report.html`. Do not edit the task's other files or any implementation files.
    32	  Reply: report path + any failure, nothing else.
    33	- For small, single-file or tightly coupled changes, recommend doing the work directly instead of forcing subagents. If the user still requests orchestration, comply.
    34	
    35	## Files
    36	
    37	Everything for one task lives in `poe/<short-task-slug>/`, relative to the current working directory (the directory the session was started in, even if that is not the repository root). Create `poe/` and the task directory if they do not exist (`mkdir -p`). Never overwrite the directory of a different task; pick a distinct slug. Slug `docs` is reserved.
    38	
    39	```
    40	poe/docs/              shared across tasks, created only when first needed (written by `grill`)
    41	  GLOSSARY.md          project terms
    42	  adr/NNNN-slug.md     architecture decision records
    43	poe/<short-task-slug>/
    44	  plan.md              what will be built and why (written by `plan`)
    45	  phases/NN-name.md    one brief per phase, listing its work units (written by `split`)
    46	  status.md            state of every phase and unit, and the next action
    47	  progress/NN-unit.md  running notes written by each worker during execution
    48	  summary.md           execution summary, overwritten at the end of each `execute`/`resume` run
    49	  report.html          step-by-step report built from the files above and logs/
    50	  logs/<session-id>/   copies of the Claude Code transcripts of each session that worked on this task
    51	    <session-id>.jsonl         main (orchestrator) transcript
    52	    subagents/agent-*.jsonl    worker transcripts
    53	    subagents/agent-*.meta.json
    54	```
    55	
    56	## Plan mode: write `plan.md`
    57	
    58	1. Inspect only the relevant repository context, instructions, tests, and environment. Use read-only exploration subagents when exploration would otherwise overwhelm parent context. Also read `poe/docs/` if present.
    59	2. Write `poe/<short-task-slug>/plan.md` from what the user wants to do: objective, scope and exclusions, assumptions, the approach, acceptance criteria, risks, and how the result will be tested or validated. This file describes the work itself; it does not mention phases, subagents, or token budgets. Keep it short: do not restate the request, and give background only where it shapes a decision.
    60	3. **Do not overengineer.** Plan the simplest approach that meets the stated requirements:
    61	   - Build only what the user asked for. No speculative features, configuration options, plugin systems, or abstraction layers added "for later".
    62	   - Prefer the tools, libraries, and patterns the repository already uses over introducing new ones.
    63	   - The resulting code must stay readable by humans: plain control flow, descriptive names, small functions, and comments only where the reason is not obvious. Prefer a few clear lines over a clever one.
    64	   - Keep the process as light as the code. Do not add steps, files, or reviews that the task does not need.
    65	4. Open decisions (the user's to make, not settleable from the code or sensible defaults) → do not guess; switch to Grill mode with the task. Otherwise write the plan in one shot.
    66	5. Show a short summary of the plan, state the path of `plan.md`, and stop. Point to the file; do not repeat its contents. The user reviews the file and may ask for changes; apply requested changes to `plan.md` and stop again. Do not proceed to the split until the user runs `split`. Reply terse: ≤5 bullet fragments, no prose, don't repeat file contents; the `Next:` block is not counted. End the reply with a `Next:` line and a fenced block holding the exact command with the full plan path, so it can be pasted into a fresh `/clear`ed session. Nothing after the block:
    67	   ````
    68	   Next:
    69	   ```
    70	   /poe:poe split poe/<short-task-slug>/plan.md
    71	   ```
    72	   ````
    73	
    74	## Grill mode: interview, then write `plan.md`
    75	
    76	1. Do Plan step 1, then read `poe/docs/` and `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/GRILLING.md`; follow GRILLING.md for rounds and writes.
    77	2. Argument is an existing `plan.md` → load it; grill only its assumptions and open or risky points. Otherwise → new slug and a `plan.md` holding only `## Decisions`.
    78	3. Ask one round, then stop. After the answers, write as GRILLING.md says.
    79	4. Frontier empty → ask the user to confirm shared understanding.
    80	5. Confirmed → write or update the full plan (Plan steps 2–3; keep `## Decisions`; link new ADRs), then reply as in Plan step 5 (`Next:` split block).
    81	6. Copy the logs (see Logs) at the end of the mode.
    82	
    83	## Split mode: split `plan.md` into phases and work units
    84	
    85	Read `plan.md` as it currently is on disk, including any edits the user made by hand. If phase briefs already exist from an earlier split and no unit has been started, replace them; if work has started, ask before changing them.
    86	
    87	1. Split the plan into ordered **phases** with explicit dependencies, and each phase into **work units**. One work unit is handled by one fresh subagent and must be independently verifiable.
    88	2. Size each unit so that one subagent can finish it in roughly 100k tokens of context, counting the files it must read, the edits, and the test output. Split a unit that looks larger; merge units that are trivially small. Use as few phases and units as the work actually needs.
    89	3. Identify which units can run in parallel because they do not modify overlapping files or share mutable state. Run dependent or overlapping units sequentially, or isolate them in separate git worktrees and integrate deliberately.
    90	4. Write one brief per phase at `phases/NN-name.md`. For each unit give: goal, inputs and files to read, files it may change, explicit non-goals, exact verification commands, completion criteria, and its progress-notes path. When `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md` or relevant `poe/docs/adr/` files exist, list them in each unit's inputs.
    91	5. Write `status.md` listing every phase and unit as pending.
    92	6. Show the phase split, state where the files are, and ask for approval. Point to the files; do not repeat their contents. Do not start implementation in `split` mode. Reply terse: ≤5 bullet fragments, no prose, don't repeat file contents; the `Next:` block is not counted. End the reply with the same `Next:` line and fenced block as Plan mode step 5, holding the execute command. Nothing after the block:
    93	   ````
    94	   Next:
    95	   ```
    96	   /poe:poe execute poe/<short-task-slug>/plan.md
    97	   ```
    98	   ````
    99	
   100	## Execute mode
   101	
   102	1. Read `plan.md`, `status.md`, and the brief of the next phase. Verify that the plan is approved and the prerequisites of the next unit are satisfied.
   103	2. Dispatch a **fresh non-fork subagent** for each work unit. Prefer the `poe:phase-worker` subagent bundled with this plugin (if it is not available under that name, look for `phase-worker`); otherwise use an appropriate built-in agent capable of doing the work. Do not use a fork for routine delegation: it inherits the parent's history.
   104	3. Give the worker only: the goal, the phase-brief path, necessary repository paths, interfaces and dependencies, allowed files, completion criteria, and its progress-notes path. Do not paste the parent conversation or large tool output.
   105	4. The worker implements or analyzes only its assigned unit and runs the relevant tests. It writes its progress notes **as it works**, not only at the end: it updates the notes file after each meaningful step, so that the notes are current if the worker stops, is compacted, or fails.
   106	5. Run independent, non-overlapping units in parallel only when safe. Never silently overwrite another agent's edits.
   107	6. Check the worker's claims against the actual files, test outputs, and git diff. For significant or high-risk changes, use a separate fresh-context reviewer before marking the unit verified. Fix or reassign failed units with a new scoped brief.
   108	7. Update `status.md` after every unit. Keep the parent response concise: phase, tests, blockers, and next action. Reference files rather than returning large transcripts or repeating file contents.
   109	   Reply terse: ≤5 bullet fragments, no prose, don't repeat file contents.
   110	8. Move to the next approved phase after verification. Stop for genuinely ambiguous requirements, security-sensitive changes, destructive operations, deployments, or decisions beyond the approved plan.
   111	9. At completion, run integration tests, review the full change set, and report what passed, what remains uncertain, and where the files were saved; point to files rather than repeating their contents. Write the same report to `summary.md` (what passed, what remains uncertain, blockers, and file locations), overwriting any earlier one; `status.md` stays the source of truth for state. Then copy the logs (see Logs) and build the report (see Report).
   112	   Reply terse: ≤10 bullet fragments, no prose, don't repeat file contents.
   113	
   114	## Logs
   115	
   116	At the end of every mode (`plan`, `grill`, `split`, `execute`, `resume`, `report`), and whenever execution stops for user input, copy this session's transcripts into the task directory:
   117	
   118	```sh
   119	dest="poe/<short-task-slug>/logs/${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}"
   120	src=$(find "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects" -name "${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}.jsonl" | head -1)
   121	mkdir -p "$dest"
   122	cp "$src" "$dest/"
   123	[ -d "${src%.jsonl}/subagents" ] && cp -R "${src%.jsonl}/subagents" "$dest/"
   124	```
   125	
   126	- Re-running it overwrites the earlier copy with the current, longer transcript, so repeating it is safe.
   127	- The copy is a snapshot: anything after it (such as the final reply of the turn) is missing until the next copy.
   128	- If the transcript cannot be found (`src` is empty or `cp` fails), say so in the reply and carry on. A missing log never blocks the task.
   129	
   130	## Report
   131	
   132	At the end of `execute` and `resume` (after `summary.md` and the log copy), and in `report` mode, build `report.html` from the task directory:
   133	
   134	```sh
   135	python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/poe_report.py" poe/<short-task-slug>
   136	```
   137	
   138	- The script writes `poe/<short-task-slug>/report.html` and prints its path. Re-running it replaces the earlier report.
   139	- If it fails (for example, `python3` is missing or the command is refused), say so in the reply and carry on. A missing report never blocks the task.
   140	
   141	## Progress notes
   142	
   143	Each worker keeps one file, `progress/NN-unit.md`, and updates it throughout its run. `resume` and any follow-on worker rely on it, so it must make sense to an agent that has seen nothing else.
   144	
   145	```
   146	# Unit ID: status (in progress | done | partial | blocked)
   147	## Done so far
   148	## Files changed or produced
   149	## Tests run and observed results
   150	## Decisions and assumptions
   151	## Next step / remaining work
   152	```
   153	
   154	When a unit is handed to a second worker, that worker reads the existing notes and continues in the same file.
   155	
   156	## Context policy: about 100k tokens per agent
   157	
   158	- 100k is a **soft target**, not a hard limit. Never claim to know exact token usage unless a tool reports it; otherwise judge by how much has been read and produced.
   159	- Hand over at a natural boundary, not at a number. When a worker nears the target, it finishes the step it is in the middle of (an edit in flight, a test run, a debugging thread that is about to resolve), then brings its progress notes up to date and returns `partial`. Going moderately over the target to finish a coherent step is correct; stopping mid-edit to respect the number is not.
   160	- The orchestrator then starts a **fresh non-fork worker** for the remainder, pointed at the progress notes. Do not keep resuming a bloated agent.
   161	- Prefer this file-based handover to automatic compaction. Automatic compaction is a backstop: it can fire in the middle of a step and loses detail, which is why the notes are kept current throughout.
   162	- Keep the parent lean: orchestration and short summaries only; delegate large searches, code reading, and log interpretation.
   163	- Avoid unnecessary parallelism, repeated repository scans, duplicate reading, and verbose inter-agent messages.
   164	
   165	## Constraints
   166	
   167	- Follow the project's `CLAUDE.md`, security practices, and user instructions.
   168	- Implement what the plan says and no more. Keep code simple and readable by humans; do not add abstractions or features the plan does not call for.

   170	- Never infer that a test passed without observing its result. Preserve unknowns rather than fabricating evidence.
   171	- If an agent has no delegation tool, say so and execute sequentially using the same file-based phase structure.

    11	
    12	## Decision tree
    13	
    14	- Task = tree of decisions. A decision depends on others when its options only make sense once they are settled.
    15	- **Frontier** = open decisions whose prerequisites are all settled. Ask only the frontier; deeper questions wait for later rounds.
    16	- `grill <plan-path>`: tree = the plan's assumptions, open points, risky points. Settled `## Decisions` entries are not re-asked.
    17	
    18	## Facts vs decisions
    19	
    20	- Facts (what the code does, what exists, versions, conventions, test setup): look them up in the code, or with read-only exploration subagents. Never ask the user.
    21	- Decisions (what the user wants, trade-offs only they can weigh): ask.
    22	- Missing detail with an obvious default = not a question. Use the default; note it under Assumptions.
    23	
    24	## Rounds
    25	
    26	- Plain text only. No AskUserQuestion.
    27	- Each round: whole frontier, numbered `Q1..Qn`. Each question: one terse line + `Rec:` recommended answer (+ short why when not obvious).
    28	- Word recommendations so "yes" accepts all of them.
    29	- Reply rules, stated once at the end of the round: "yes" = accept all recs; override by number (e.g. `Q2: no, keep flat files`); unmentioned = rec accepted.
    30	- Then stop and wait for the reply.
    31	- Recommendations follow SKILL.md Plan step 3 "Do not overengineer": simplest option meeting the stated need, repo's existing tools/patterns, no speculative features or config.
    32	- Skip trivia: no question whose answer would not change the plan. A clear task may need one round or none.
    33	
    34	Format:
    35	```
    36	Round N
    37	Q1. <question>
    38	    Rec: <answer>
    39	Q2. ...
    40	Reply "yes" to accept all, or override by number.
    41	```
    42	
    43	## Domain modeling
    44	
    45	While grilling, sharpen the language:
    46	- Term used loosely, or two words for one thing → ask which one and what exactly it means.
    47	- Probe a term with a concrete edge-case scenario ("note edited after archiving: still archived?").
    48	- Check terms against existing code names and `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md`; flag conflicts.
    49	
    50	## Writing after every round
    51	
    52	After each answered round, before asking the next:
    53	1. Append the settled decisions to `## Decisions` in `poe/<slug>/plan.md` (one bullet each: decision + short why).
    54	2. Add or update glossary entries for terms resolved this round.
    55	3. Write an ADR for any decision that qualifies (below).
    56	
    57	Nothing settled lives only in the chat; `/clear` then `grill <plan-path>` must resume without re-asking.
    58	
    59	## Glossary
    60	
    61	- Path: `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md`. Create only when the first term is resolved.
    62	- Project-specific terms only. No generic programming words. No implementation detail (file names, classes, schemas).
    63	- Entry format:
    64	  ```
    65	  **Term**: 1–2 sentence definition.
    66	  _Avoid_: synonym, other synonym
    67	  ```
    68	- Keep entries alphabetical; edit an existing entry instead of adding a duplicate.
    69	
    70	## ADRs
    71	
    72	- Path: `poe/docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md`. Create `adr/` only when the first ADR is written.
    73	- Write one only when all three hold:
    74	  1. Hard to reverse (costly to change later).
    75	  2. Surprising (a future reader would ask "why this way?").
    76	  3. Real trade-off (viable alternatives were rejected).
    77	- Otherwise the decision lives only in `plan.md` `## Decisions`. Zero ADRs is normal.
    78	- Number = highest existing number + 1, 4 digits (`0001` if none). Slug = short kebab-case title.
    79	- Format:
    80	  ```
    81	  # NNNN: <Title>
    82	
    83	  <1–3 sentences: context, decision, why.>
    84	  ```
    85	  Add sections (Considered options, Consequences) only when they add real value.
    86	
    87	## Finish
    88	
    89	- Frontier empty → summarize understanding in ≤5 bullets; ask the user to confirm it matches theirs.
    90	- Correction → new round on the affected decisions.
    91	- Confirmed → grilling done; continue Grill mode in SKILL.md.

     9	
    10	User request: $ARGUMENTS

    15	
    16	Be concise. Sacrifice grammar for the sake of concision.

    21	- Never drop required content: acceptance criteria, risks, verification commands, exact file paths, test results, unknowns.

    27	- `split [plan-path]`: split a reviewed `plan.md` into phases and work units, then stop for user approval. Do not edit implementation files.
    28	- `execute [plan-path]`: execute a plan that has been split and approved. If the plan has no phase briefs yet, say so and ask the user to run `split` first.

    41	  GLOSSARY.md          project terms
    42	  adr/NNNN-slug.md     architecture decision records
    43	poe/<short-task-slug>/
    44	  plan.md              what will be built and why (written by `plan`)
    45	  phases/NN-name.md    one brief per phase, listing its work units (written by `split`)
    46	  status.md            state of every phase and unit, and the next action
    47	  progress/NN-unit.md  running notes written by each worker during execution
    48	  summary.md           execution summary, overwritten at the end of each `execute`/`resume` run
    49	  report.html          step-by-step report built from the files above and logs/
    50	  logs/<session-id>/   copies of the Claude Code transcripts of each session that worked on this task
    51	    <session-id>.jsonl         main (orchestrator) transcript
    52	    subagents/agent-*.jsonl    worker transcripts
    53	    subagents/agent-*.meta.json
    54	```
    55	
    56	## Plan mode: write `plan.md`
    57	
    58	1. Inspect only the relevant repository context, instructions, tests, and environment. Use read-only exploration subagents when exploration would otherwise overwhelm parent context. Also read `poe/docs/` if present.
    59	2. Write `poe/<short-task-slug>/plan.md` from what the user wants to do: objective, scope and exclusions, assumptions, the approach, acceptance criteria, risks, and how the result will be tested or validated. This file describes the work itself; it does not mention phases, subagents, or token budgets. Keep it short: do not restate the request, and give background only where it shapes a decision.
    60	3. **Do not overengineer.** Plan the simplest approach that meets the stated requirements:
    61	   - Build only what the user asked for. No speculative features, configuration options, plugin systems, or abstraction layers added "for later".
    62	   - Prefer the tools, libraries, and patterns the repository already uses over introducing new ones.
    63	   - The resulting code must stay readable by humans: plain control flow, descriptive names, small functions, and comments only where the reason is not obvious. Prefer a few clear lines over a clever one.

    86	
    87	1. Split the plan into ordered **phases** with explicit dependencies, and each phase into **work units**. One work unit is handled by one fresh subagent and must be independently verifiable.

    95	   ```

    97	   ```
    98	   ````

1	# poe: phase orchestrator for Claude Code
     2	
     3	A Claude Code plugin with one skill (`poe`) and one subagent (`phase-worker`). It plans a task, splits it into work units sized for about 100k tokens each, and runs each unit in a fresh-context subagent that keeps file-based progress notes.
     4	
     5	Requires Claude Code v2.1.296 or later.
     6	
     7	## Installation
     8	
     9	This repository is both the plugin and its own marketplace. Add the marketplace, then install the plugin:
    10	
    11	```sh
    12	claude plugin marketplace add sreejancodes/poe
    13	claude plugin install poe@poe-tools
    14	```
    15	
    16	The same commands work inside a session as `/plugin marketplace add sreejancodes/poe` and `/plugin install poe@poe-tools`. Then run `/reload-plugins` or start a new session.
    17	
    18	By default the plugin is installed at **user** scope, so it is available in every project. Add `--scope project` to enable it only for the current repository, recorded in `.claude/settings.json`.
    19	
    20	### Update and uninstall
    21	
    22	Third-party marketplaces do not update automatically. To get the latest version:
    23	
    24	```sh
    25	claude plugin marketplace update poe-tools
    26	claude plugin update poe@poe-tools
    27	```
    28	
    29	To remove it:
    30	
    31	```sh
    32	claude plugin uninstall poe@poe-tools
    33	claude plugin marketplace remove poe-tools
    34	```
    35	
    36	### Offering it to everyone on a project
    37	
    38	Commit this to the project's `.claude/settings.json`:
    39	
    40	```json
    41	{
    42	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    43	    "poe-tools": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "sreejancodes/poe" } }
    44	  },
    45	  "enabledPlugins": { "poe@poe-tools": true }
    46	}
    47	```
    48	
    49	Once a collaborator trusts the folder, the marketplace is registered for them. They still need to run `claude plugin install poe@poe-tools --scope project` once.
    50	
    51	## Usage
    52	
    53	Plugin skills are namespaced, so the command is `/poe:poe`:
    54	
    55	```text
    56	/poe:poe plan Build an HPV ORF analysis pipeline with tests and reproducible outputs
    57	/poe:poe grill Build an HPV ORF analysis pipeline with tests and reproducible outputs
    58	/poe:poe grill poe/hpv-orf-analysis/plan.md
    59	/poe:poe split poe/hpv-orf-analysis/plan.md
    60	/poe:poe execute poe/hpv-orf-analysis/plan.md
    61	/poe:poe resume poe/hpv-orf-analysis/plan.md
    62	/poe:poe report poe/hpv-orf-analysis/plan.md
    63	```
    64	
    65	- **Plan** writes `plan.md` from what you asked for, keeping the approach simple and the code human-readable, then stops. Review the file, edit it or ask for changes, and repeat until you are happy with it. If it finds open decisions that only you can make, it switches to grill instead of guessing.
    66	- **Grill** interviews you before planning. Each round asks numbered questions, each with a recommended answer; reply "yes" to accept all, or override by number. `grill <task>` starts from scratch and writes `plan.md` once you confirm; `grill <plan-path>` questions an existing plan's assumptions and open points and updates it in place. Decisions are added to `plan.md` under `## Decisions` every round; project terms and hard-to-reverse decisions go to the shared `poe/docs/`.
    67	- **Split** takes the reviewed `plan.md` and splits it into phases and work units, each sized for one subagent at roughly 100k tokens. It then stops for approval.
    68	- **Execute** hands each work unit to a fresh `poe:phase-worker` subagent, which writes progress notes as it works. The orchestrator verifies each unit before moving on.
    69	- **Resume** uses the status file and progress notes to continue safely.
    70	- **Report** copies the session's logs and (re)builds `report.html`, a step-by-step view of what the orchestrator and each worker did. Execute and resume also build it automatically at the end, after `summary.md` and the log copy; if the build fails, the reply says so and the task carries on.
    71	
    72	Use `plan` when the task is clear. Use `grill` when you want to be interviewed, or to challenge a draft plan.
    73	
    74	Output is deliberately terse: replies point to files instead of repeating them, and plan and split replies end with the next command to paste.
    75	
    76	## Files
    77

"""Tiny notes CLI: add, list, show notes stored as JSON."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

NOTES_FILE = Path("notes.json")


def load_notes():
    if not NOTES_FILE.exists():
        return []
    return json.loads(NOTES_FILE.read_text())


def save_notes(notes):
    NOTES_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(notes, indent=2))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Notes CLI")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    add = sub.add_parser("add")
    add.add_argument("text")
    sub.add_parser("list")
    show = sub.add_parser("show")
    show.add_argument("index", type=int)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    notes = load_notes()
    if args.command == "add":
        notes.append({"text": args.text})
        save_notes(notes)
    elif args.command == "list":
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(i, note["text"])
    elif args.command == "show":
        print(notes[args.index]["text"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    if not NOTES_FILE.exists():
        return []
    return json.loads(NOTES_FILE.read_text())


def save_notes(notes):
    NOTES_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(notes, indent=2))


def main():

    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    add = sub.add_parser("add")
    add.add_argument("text")
    sub.add_parser("list")
    show = sub.add_parser("show")
    show.add_argument("index", type=int)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    notes = load_notes()
    if args.command == "add":
        notes.append({"text": args.text})
        save_notes(notes)
    elif args.command == "list":
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(i, note["text"])
    elif args.command == "show":
        print(notes[args.index]["text"])

# Plan: `--verbose` flag for `cli.py`

## Objective
- Global `-v/--verbose` flag; when set, print diagnostic messages about what the CLI is doing.

## Scope
- In: `cli.py` (flag + messages), `test_cli.py` (tests).
- Out: log levels/`-vv`, log files, config/env vars, changes to normal output, new dependencies.

## Assumptions (not specified by request — change here if wrong)
- Flag is global, before subcommand: `python cli.py -v list`. Not repeated on each subparser.
- Verbose output → **stderr**, so stdout of `list`/`show` stays unchanged and pipeable.
- Messages (one line each):
  - notes file path + whether it exists
  - number of notes loaded
  - action taken: note added (new count) and file saved / listing N notes / showing note at index
- Default (no flag): output byte-identical to today.

## Approach
- Use stdlib `logging` (no new deps):
  - `parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", help=...)` on the top-level parser.
  - After parsing: `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING, format="%(message)s")` — basicConfig writes to stderr.
  - Module-level `log = logging.getLogger(__name__)`; `log.info(...)` calls in `main()` around load/save/each command.
- Keep `load_notes`/`save_notes` signatures unchanged (existing test calls `load_notes()`).

## Acceptance criteria
- `python cli.py --help` lists `-v, --verbose`.
- `python cli.py -v list` prints diagnostics to stderr; stdout identical to `python cli.py list`.
- `python cli.py -v add "x"` reports load count, add, save on stderr.
- Without `-v`: no stderr output; stdout unchanged.
- Existing test passes; new tests pass.

## Risks
- `logging.basicConfig` is a no-op if root logger already configured (e.g. in tests) → tests should capture via `assertLogs` or call `main()` with patched `sys.argv` in a temp dir.
- Tests touching `notes.json` must use a temp dir / patch `cli.NOTES_FILE` to avoid writing in repo.
- `-v` placed after subcommand (`cli.py list -v`) will error — accepted; documented in `--help` via top-level parser.

## Validation
- Add tests in `test_cli.py` (unittest, patch `sys.argv` + `cli.NOTES_FILE` to temp path):
  - verbose `list` emits INFO logs (`assertLogs`); stdout unchanged.
  - non-verbose `list` emits no INFO logs.
- Run: `python3 -m unittest -v test_cli`
- Manual: `python3 cli.py -v add hi`, `python3 cli.py -v list 2>/dev/null` (stdout only), `python3 cli.py list` (no stderr).

# Plan: archive old notes

## Decisions
- "Old" = age: `add` records a `created` date; a note is old when it is older than N days. Why: notes have no date today, and age is the plain meaning of "old".
- Archiving is manual: new `archive --older-than DAYS` subcommand. Nothing is archived automatically. Why: the simplest option, with no surprises on other commands.
- Archived notes stay in `notes.json` with an `archived` flag; `list` hides them. Why: user choice; keeps a single data file.
- No commands to view or restore archived notes. Why: not requested.
- Notes with no `created` date (added before this change) are never archived. Why: their age is unknown; skipping them is the safe choice.
- `list` shows each note's real position in the file (numbers may have gaps); `show N` works for any note, archived or not. Why: keeps `show` pointing at the same note.
- `created` = UTC ISO 8601 timestamp; age compared to the exact time (`now - created > DAYS days`). Why: simplest exact comparison; no date-boundary ambiguity.
- `archive` output: prints `Archived K notes`. `show` prints text only, no archived marker. Why: user confirmed defaults.

## Objective
- Let the user hide notes older than N days from `list` via a manual `archive` command, keeping them stored. Terms: see `poe/docs/GLOSSARY.md` (Old note, Archived note).

## Scope
- In: `cli.py` (`add`, `list`, new `archive`), `test_cli.py`.
- Out: auto-archiving, viewing/restoring archived notes, `--dry-run`, showing dates in `list`, editing notes, new dependencies, migrating old notes.

## Assumptions
- `--older-than` required; argparse `type=int`; negative → error (`parser.error`). 0 allowed (archives every dated note older than now).
- Already-archived notes are skipped and not counted in K.
- Missing `archived` key = not archived (old notes have neither key).
- `show N` with bad index keeps current behaviour (unchanged).

## Approach
- Stdlib only: `datetime`, `timezone`, `timedelta`.
- `add`: `notes.append({"text": ..., "created": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()})`.
- Small helper `is_old(note, days, now)`: `False` if no `created`; else `now - datetime.fromisoformat(note["created"]) > timedelta(days=days)`.
- `archive`: `now` read once; for each note not archived and `is_old` → set `note["archived"] = True`, count; `save_notes` only if count > 0; print `Archived {count} notes`.
- `list`: keep `enumerate`; skip notes with `note.get("archived")`.
- `show`: unchanged.
- Keep `load_notes`/`save_notes` signatures (existing test).
- Note: `poe/verbose-flag` plan also edits `cli.py`/`test_cli.py`; whichever lands second must merge, not overwrite.

## Acceptance criteria
- `python3 cli.py add x` stores a note with `text` and a UTC ISO `created`.
- `python3 cli.py archive --older-than N` flags only dated, unarchived notes older than N days; prints `Archived K notes`.
- Notes without `created` are never archived.
- `list` omits archived notes; shown numbers are real file indexes (gaps allowed).
- `show N` prints text of any note, archived or not.
- `archive` without `--older-than` or with a negative value exits with an argparse error.
- Existing and new tests pass.

## Risks
- `datetime.fromisoformat` on Python < 3.11 can't parse `Z` suffix — avoided by writing via `isoformat()` (`+00:00`). Any hand-edited bad date would raise; accepted (not in scope).
- Tests must not touch repo `notes.json` → patch `cli.NOTES_FILE` to a temp path.
- Time-dependent tests → build notes with explicit `created` values relative to `now` (well clear of the boundary), or pass `now` to `is_old`.
- Conflict with `verbose-flag` work in same files (see Approach).

## Validation
- Tests in `test_cli.py` (unittest; patch `sys.argv` + `cli.NOTES_FILE` to temp file; capture stdout):
  - `add` writes `created` parseable as UTC datetime.
  - `is_old` boundary: just under / just over N days with fixed `now`.
  - `archive` skips undated and already-archived notes; output count correct.
  - `list` hides archived notes and keeps index gaps.
  - `show` on archived note prints its text.
  - negative `--older-than` → `SystemExit`.
- Run: `python3 -m unittest -v test_cli`
- Manual (temp dir): `python3 cli.py add a`; edit `created` to 40 days ago; `python3 cli.py archive --older-than 30` → `Archived 1 notes`; `python3 cli.py list` hides it; `python3 cli.py show 0` prints it.
